paper.title: LNUCB-TA: Linear-nonlinear Hybrid Bandit Learning with Temporal Attention

settings.name_in_paper: Hybrid contextual MAB problem (linear + k-NN reward in joint context/reward-history space)
unmapped: A finite arms with per-arm linear parameter plus a k-NN term computed from each arm's own reward history
Noise bounded in absolute value by sigma
Expected reward depends on past observed rewards (history-dependent), so not strictly i.i.d. rewards
settings.definition_quote: We consider a hybrid contextual MAB problem within a metric space (X x Z, rho) ... The reward corresponding to each arm a for a given context x_t at time t is denoted as a random variable Y_t^a, constrained within the interval [-1,1] ... o^a_t(x_t^a, z_t^a) = E[Y_t^a | X_t = x_t, Z_t = z_t] = l^a_t(x_t^a) + f_{k,t}^a(x_t^a, z_t^a) ... The feature vector X_t is drawn i.i.d. from a fixed marginal distribution D over X.

symbols.U_sum: sum_a T^a (u_{t,k}^a)^2, sum of squared k-NN uncertainties weighted by pull counts
symbols.sigma: bound on |xi_t^a| (paper also calls sigma^2 total variance of linear and k-NN components)

conditions: ||x|| <= B (L_feat) for all x in D
tuning: beta_t^a = sigma^2(2 + 4d log(1 + T B^2 W^2/d + sum_a T^a (u_{t,k}^a)^2/d) + 8 log(4/delta))

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Suppose the noise |\xi_t^a| is bounded by \sigma ..., the true parameter vector (\mu^a)^* has a norm bounded by W ..., and the context vectors x are bounded such that \|x\| \leq B ..., and let \lambda = \sigma^2/W^2. ... with probability greater than 1-\delta, for all t \geq 0, R_T \leq b \sigma \sqrt{T ( d \log ( 1 + \frac{TB^2 W^2}{d \sigma^2} + \frac{\sum_{a=1}^A T^a (u_{t,k}^a)^2}{d \sigma^2} ) + \log ( \frac{4}{\delta} ) )}

results.notes: Regret defined via realized rewards Y against per-round oracle. Paper's B renamed L_feat, W renamed S. Proof is non-rigorous; the bound depends on data-dependent k-NN uncertainties. Setting mapping is approximate.

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Given these conditions, the simplified regret bound for LNUCB-TA is R_T = \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{dT \log T}), which, by absorbing logarithmic factors into \tilde{\mathcal{O}}, we can state: R_T = \tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{dT}).

results.notes: Simplified form of r1; also stated as O~(sqrt(dT)). Suppresses sigma, B, W and k-NN uncertainty terms.
